title: The second of the five propositions is not Jansenius's
source_text: IX. Ex quibus apparet falso Jansenio tribui propositionem illam, Interiori gratiae in statu naturae lapsae nunquam resistitur. Quae tamen secunda est quinque famosarum propositionum, quae tanquam Jansenii Episcopi Iprensis, ut haereticae damnatae sunt a Pontificibus Romanis Innocentio X. & Alexandro VII. constitutionibus ea de re editis. Praeterquam enim quod ejus propositionis verba in operibus viri illius nullibi leguntur, contrarium expresse docet loco modo citato, ubi diserte affirmat quod constet multos divinitus mente collustrari, imo vero & in ipsa voluntate motibus divinae gratiae percelli, qui tamen ab ejus interna suasione & inclinatione dissentiunt.
pass_a_gloss: IX. From which it appears that falsely is attributed to Jansenius that proposition, Interior grace in the state of fallen nature is never resisted. Which however is the second of the five famous propositions, which as of Jansenius Bishop of Ypres, were condemned as heretical by the Roman Pontiffs Innocent X. and Alexander VII. by constitutions issued on that matter. For besides that the words of that proposition are nowhere read in the works of that man, he expressly teaches the contrary in the place just cited, where he distinctly affirms that it is established that many are divinely enlightened in mind, nay indeed also in the will itself are struck by motions of divine grace, who however dissent from its inner persuasion and inclination.
pass_b_english: Thesis IX. This shows that Jansenius is wrongly credited with the proposition: 'In the state of fallen nature, inward grace is never resisted.' Yet this is the second of the five notorious propositions that the Roman pontiffs Innocent X and Alexander VII condemned as heretical, as being those of Jansenius, bishop of Ypres, in constitutions they issued on the matter.

Apart from the fact that the wording of this proposition appears nowhere in his works, he plainly teaches the opposite in the passage just quoted, where he states outright that many people are, by God's doing, given light in their minds and even stirred in their wills by movements of divine grace, and yet refuse consent to its inward persuasion and leaning.

lemmas.latin: Interiori gratiae in statu naturae lapsae nunquam resistitur
lemmas.gloss: Interior grace in the state of fallen nature is never resisted

choices.why: Famosus here has its common Neo-Latin sense of 'much talked-of, notorious'.

bible_refs: The five propositions, condemned by Innocent X, Cum occasione (31 May 1653), and Alexander VII, Ad sanctam beati Petri sedem (16 October 1656).
Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris.
